subject: QBR slate review: product & engineering timeline gaps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: QBR slate review: product & engineering timeline gaps

Team — putting this thread together to lock the QBR slate and surface any timing risks we need to elevate to execs. High level ask: review the sheet attached and the doc linked below, call out any gaps that would force us to move a launch target or require an ask from GTM/ops.

Priority checklist (please reply inline or leave comments in the doc):
- Confirm feature slate for Nov–Dec launch window (what is committed vs. contingency)
- Identify top 3 delivery risks (impact + mitigation + owner)
- Confirm marketing/go-to-market hard dates that are non-negotiable

Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2BqbrSlAtE_QBR-Slate (QBR slate v2)
Attachment: qbr_slate_v2.xlsx

Quick notes: marketing told me they need final copy by 2026-11-24 to hit our public cadence; product should call blockers early. I'll collate and present an exec-ready slide for Thurs QBR prep.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR slate review: product & engineering timeline gaps

Priya — thanks for pulling this together. Quick pass from delivery/ops perspective.

Top delivery risks I see (high level):
1) Model verticalization for personalization (impact: high) — we still need 1 perf iteration on the new quantized kernel; if that slips we degrade latency SLOs for high-throughput customers. Mitigation: keep previous quantized profile available as fallback; owner: Karthik.
2) Front-end integration for rollout gating (impact: medium) — current backlog on the feature flags implementation. Mitigation: staggered rollout + feature flag toggles; owner: Marcus.
3) Third-party marketplace certification (impact: medium-low) — pending privacy attestation from partner. Mitigation: prioritize required doc sign-off; owner: Lauren.

I attached a short risk matrix I'm working through (delivery_risks_v1.pdf). My recommendation: we classify the model verticalization as "must mitigate" and discuss a short canary plan in the QBR decisions slide.

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR slate review: product & engineering timeline gaps

Adding product constraints and GTM inputs. Marketing confirmed the creative freeze is 2026-11-24; any feature that is not stable by then will not have the full launch marketing. That effectively makes 2026-11-18 the last date for engineering signoff on any visible UX changes (to allow QA + localization).

Implications and proposed mitigations:
- If model verticalization requires more than one perf iteration, we should ship the base personalization rollout with the existing model and plan verticalized improvements as a phased release (Nov -> Jan).
- For features requiring cross-service schema changes, put a hard dependency cut on 2026-11-12 and scope remaining work into a follow-up release.
- Action items: Marcus to confirm feature-flag readiness by 11/12; Karthik to provide perf-validation ETA by 11/12 end of day; Vivek to produce an exec-friendly risk slide by 11/13.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR slate review: product & engineering timeline gaps

Quick engineering update and clarification on the perf work: the PR that enables the new quantized kernel landed yesterday (PR #1048) but we still need to run the 72-hour perf soak and the load-validation suite against the recovery path. Current ETA for finishing validation is 11/12 EOD (assuming no regressions). If the soak finds regressions we estimate an additional 3–5 working days to remediate and re-run.

Contingency plan I recommend:
- Keep the previous quantized binary pinned on production (fallback) until perf soak passes.
- Prepare a canary plan limited to 5% traffic with auto-rollback based on latency and error thresholds (I can draft canary steps).

Jira: https://company.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-3421

Thanks — Acme team here. We appreciate the transparency. From our side, 2026-11-30 is the date we committed to for the public feature in our roadmap; moving beyond that will cause internal customer escalation. Two asks from Acme: (1) can you confirm whether a canary (5%) with rollback will be an acceptable mitigation for any perf risk, and (2) please call out any residual functional differences the phased rollout would have vs. the fully verticalized model.
